description: Robust dictionary matching via normalized substring-contains instead of exact whole-line match, so known terms (skill names, etc.) translate even when Tesseract reads the line with different spacing/newlines or as a fragment. Touches bronco_ocr.dll (dictionary + translator). Independent of FEAT-002 (which touches d3d11.dll overlay).
steps: In src/translation/dictionary.h: change the private static std::string normalize(const std::string&) contract to lowercasing + collapsing every run of whitespace (space, tab, CR, newline) to a single space + trimming leading/trailing space. Keep it static. Add a new public method declaration: std::optional<std::string> lookupContains(const std::string& sourceText) const; with a doc comment explaining it finds the LONGEST dictionary key whose normalized form is a substring of the normalized sourceText (or the sourceText normalized is a substring of the key), requiring the matched key normalized length >= 4 characters.

In src/translation/dictionary.cpp: rewrite normalize() to lowercase, then collapse any run of isspace() characters into a single ASCII space, and trim leading/trailing space. Ensure loadFromFile() keeps storing keys via this same normalize() (it already calls normalize(entry["en"])), so keys are stored whitespace-collapsed and lowercased.

In src/translation/dictionary.cpp: keep the existing exact lookup() (fast unordered_map find on normalized text) as a first-pass fast path. Implement the new lookupContains(): normalize the sourceText once; if empty return nullopt; iterate all m_entries, and for each entry whose stored (already-normalized) key length >= 4, test whether the normalized sourceText contains the key OR the key contains the normalized sourceText; among all such matches, keep the one with the LONGEST key; return its value, else nullopt. Include <optional> usage already present. A linear scan over entries per line is acceptable for now (note performance in a comment).

In src/translation/dictionary.cpp DictionaryManager::translate(const std::string& sourceText): for each category dictionary, first try dict.lookup(sourceText) (exact) then dict.lookupContains(sourceText); prefer the FIRST category that yields any match, and within a single dictionary prefer exact over contains. Return the matched translated string. Keep the second overload translate(sourceText, category) using lookup+lookupContains on that one dictionary. This keeps DictionaryManager the single routing point so Translator needs no structural change.

In src/translation/translator.cpp Translator::translate(): it already calls m_dictionaries.translate(sourceText) and sets matched=true on a hit; confirm this still compiles and that the LRU cache keyed by sourceText still works (cache stores the resolved TranslationResult). No signature change needed. Re-read the whole function to confirm identifiers are in scope.

In src/ocr/ocr_api.cpp: confirm the existing per-line loop still routes each trimmed line through handle->translator.translate(line) and sets matched=1 on hit / raw fallback (original==translated, matched=0) on miss. No structural change expected; just re-verify after the dictionary changes.

Re-read dictionary.h and dictionary.cpp end-to-end: confirm every new/changed signature in the .cpp matches a declaration in the .h, includes are sufficient (<optional>, <string>, <cctype>, <algorithm>), braces balance, and no undeclared identifiers.
acceptance_criteria: Dictionary::normalize collapses all whitespace runs (including newlines and tabs) to a single space, lowercases, and trims; keys are stored using this normalize in loadFromFile.

Dictionary::lookupContains is declared in dictionary.h and defined in dictionary.cpp, returns the longest normalized-key match (key contained in source or source contained in key) with key length >= 4, else nullopt.
DictionaryManager::translate tries exact lookup then lookupContains across categories and returns a match for inputs like an OCR line containing 'Plaguelands' among other noise.
Translator::translate still sets matched=true only on a dictionary hit and caches the result; no header signature changed.
bronco_ocr.dll sources (dictionary, translator, ocr_api) are internally consistent: no .cpp signature lacks a .h declaration, no block-scoped variable used out of scope.
verification: Cannot build on this Linux sandbox (Windows MSVC/vcpkg). Verify by reading: dictionary.h declares lookupContains and the updated normalize contract; dictionary.cpp defines both and DictionaryManager::translate routes exact-then-contains; translator.cpp and ocr_api.cpp still compile against the unchanged public translate() signature.
Confirm data/dictionaries/pt-br/skills.json contains a 'Plaguelands' entry (read-only check) so a substring match is demonstrably possible; do NOT modify the dictionary.
findings:
REVIEW v1 (NEEDS_CHANGES) follow-up — tightened the fuzzy matcher in src/translation/dictionary.{h,cpp} only (imgui_overlay.cpp and all dictionary JSON left untouched per briefing). (Issue 1) lookupContains no longer matches common short skill-name verbs against any line: a key now qualifies only if it is 'substantial' — multi-word (contains a space) with normalized length >= 6, OR a single word of length >= 8 — and it must occur on WORD BOUNDARIES within the source (bounded by a space or string start/end on each side) via the new static helper Dictionary::containsOnWordBoundary, so 'leap' matches 'use leap now' but not 'leaping'/'please'. (Issue 2) DROPPED the key-contains-source direction entirely; only source-contains-key remains, so a tiny OCR fragment can no longer claim a much longer multi-word key. (Issue 3) DictionaryManager::translate(sourceText) now iterates a FIXED priority order (Skills, Items, NpcDialogues) and runs a GLOBAL exact pass across all categories first, returning only on an exact hit, then a GLOBAL fuzzy pass in the same order — so a fuzzy hit can no longer shadow an exact hit in another category, and results are deterministic despite m_dictionaries being an unordered_map. The two-arg translate(sourceText, category) overload is unchanged (single dict, exact-then-fuzzy). (Issue 4) NOT a code change: ~348 skill entries have translated == en (e.g. Plaguelands -> Plaguelands); flagged as a dictionary-data quality follow-up for the orchestrator, no JSON modified in this run. New method containsOnWordBoundary is declared in dictionary.h (private static) and defined in dictionary.cpp; lookupContains doc contract in the header updated to describe the strict rule; includes (<optional>,<string>,<cctype>,<algorithm>) sufficient; braces balance; no block-scoped variable used out of scope (kPriority is a function-local static constexpr array; bestValue/bestKeyLen at function scope). Cannot compile on this Linux sandbox (Windows MSVC/vcpkg); CI builds on tag push.

ORIGINAL IMPLEMENTATION NOTES: Implemented in src/translation/dictionary.{h,cpp} only; translator.cpp and ocr_api.cpp needed NO changes (they already call the unchanged public translate() signatures, and ocr_api's per-line loop still routes each trimmed line through translator.translate -> DictionaryManager::translate). Changes: (1) Dictionary::normalize rewritten to lowercase + collapse every whitespace run (space/tab/CR/newline via std::isspace) to a single ASCII space + trim leading/trailing, single-pass, kept static; loadFromFile stores keys through this same normalize. (2) Added public Dictionary::lookupContains: normalizes source once, returns nullopt if empty, linear-scans m_entries, considers only stored keys of length >= 4, matches when normalized source contains the key OR the key contains the normalized source, and returns the value of the LONGEST matching key (bestValue/bestKeyLen at function scope, no out-of-scope vars). Performance tradeoff of the linear scan (~6000 entries/line) noted in a comment. (3) DictionaryManager::translate(sourceText) now tries dict.lookup (exact) then dict.lookupContains per category, returning the first category to match; the (sourceText, category) overload does the same on one dict. This keeps DictionaryManager as the single routing point so Translator::translate is unchanged and its LruCache keyed by sourceText still caches the resolved TranslationResult (matched=true only on hit). Verified data/dictionaries/pt-br/skills.json has a 'Plaguelands' entry (grep on host; note the workspace grep tool skipped it, likely gitignored, but shell grep confirmed). Correctness checked by reading: includes (<optional> via header, <string>, <cctype>, <algorithm>) sufficient, every .cpp signature has a matching .h declaration, braces balance, no undeclared identifiers, no block-scoped variable used out of scope (the prior C2065 class of bug avoided). Cannot compile on this Linux sandbox (Windows MSVC/vcpkg); CI builds on tag push. FEAT-002 (overlay clean-up + Right-CTRL-only drag) intentionally untouched.
